# ADR-051b — Amendment to ADR-051: Google Health moves to its own Google Cloud project `personal-os-health` (single-project rule superseded for Health only)

**Status:** Locked

<!-- Decision text below is verbatim from the pre-split docs/DECISIONS.md table row (2026-09-16). Do not edit a Locked decision without explicit owner approval. -->

**Amendment to ADR-051 (2026-09-01, Checkpoint 7.8B, owner-approved): Google Health moves to its OWN Google Cloud project, `personal-os-health`. ADR-051's single-project rule is superseded for Health only, because a provider policy makes it impossible to satisfy otherwise.** ADR-051 forbade any second OAuth application, client, project, account or credential set, and ADR-053a reaffirmed it. **That is no longer achievable, and the reason is a Google constraint rather than a preference.** ADR-053a fixed grant destruction by making consent additive (`include_granted_scopes=true`), and the Gmail and Calendar grants then survived correctly. But the Google Health API **rejects any token carrying scopes beyond its own**: three live consent attempts each returned `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` with reason **`DISALLOWED_OAUTH_SCOPES`** and domain `health.googleapis.com`, refused at `users/me/identity` before any data call. The two constraints are mutually exclusive while Gmail and Health share one consent screen: `false` destroys the other grants, `true` produces a token Health refuses. **The evidence is symmetric and decisive.** When Health last worked (2026-08-30) its stored `granted_scope` was exactly the three Health scopes and nothing else; meanwhile Google Calendar ran throughout on a token whose grant included `calendar.events`, `calendar.calendarlist`, `openid`, `userinfo.email` **and** `gmail.metadata`, with 30+ successful syncs an hour. Only Health is restrictive — almost certainly a deliberate Restricted-API data-protection rule preventing one token from bridging health data with mail and calendar data. **Scope of the exception.** A second project exists for Health ALONE. `personal-os-196cf` keeps Gmail and Calendar and is unchanged. There is still exactly one Google account, one credential per integration, no second account, and no reuse of a token minted for one integration by another — ADR-051's actual security intent is preserved; only its single-project mechanism is superseded. The new project mirrors the old: External audience, **In production**, unverified under the documented personal-use exception (0 of 100 users), exactly the three `.readonly` Health scopes as restricted, no sensitive or non-sensitive scopes, one Web client `Personal OS Health Web` with one redirect URI and no JavaScript origins. **`include_granted_scopes=true` is RETAINED for Health** even though its project now grants nothing else: it is harmless where there is nothing to inherit, and it keeps the integration correct if that project ever gains a second scope. **Verified live**: consent succeeded, `granted_scope` came back as exactly the three Health scopes, the same connection row was rebound with `created_at` preserved, and a manual pass ran **24 of 24 streams succeeded, 0 failed**, closing the data gap to 0 days behind. **Costs accepted and recorded**: the privacy-policy URL debt from ADR-051/6.7A is now reproduced in a second project and remains unfixed; and the three Health scopes granted to the OLD app during the failed attempts are now vestigial, removable only by revoking that app's whole grant and re-consenting Gmail and Calendar (Checkpoint 7.8B, user-approved 2026-09-01)
